messages.subject: sqldf in reference class
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sqldf team.
We recently found an issue when we runned this sqldf code into an R Reference class:

dfcount = sqldf('select term_id, count(STRING_id) as proteins from ann group by term_id', stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

The issue seems caused by the fact that "proteins" is also the name of a variable of the reference class (of type data.frame).  The issue arises when such a variable is not initialized.
We could easily fix the issue on our side, simply changing the name "proteins" with "proteinsCount", and then renaming back the variable in the resulting data frame in an additional line of code.

Thankyou for the attention and for the nice package.
Andrea

messages.subject: error in reference class
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sqldf team,

We have recently identified an issue using the newest version of your package (downloaded about 10 days ago) with the R Reference classes.

We instantiated a reference class containing a global variable called "proteins" (type data.frame).

Our code gave an error on the following line:

dfcount = suppressWarnings(sqldf('select term_id, count(STRING_id) as proteins from ann group by term_id', stringsAsFactors=FALSE))

We noticed the error to be caused by our choice of the name "proteins" for the count.  We could easily fix the issue just choosing another name.
Apparently there exists a conflict with the global variable in the reference class that has the same name (and this conflict happen only if such a global variable is NOT instantiated).

Thankyou for the attention.
Andrea Franceschini

messages.subject: RAW() can only be applied to a 'raw', not a 'double'
messages.subject_clean: RAW() can only be applied to a 'raw', not a 'double'
messages.body_plain:
I've run into this error fairly frequently and had difficulty determining why it occurs and what to do about it via Google. I also didn't see anything about what causes this error or what to do about it on the official sqldf FAQ page.

The following statement generates the error: RAW() can only be applied to a 'raw', not a 'double'.

sqldf(c("update dta set dta.FICO = dta.FICO_Score__c where dta.FICO = 0 and dta.FICO_Score__c != 0", "select * from dta"))

What I'm trying to do is update those values in a vector where the existing value is zero and another field is not zero.

My data has the form:

FICO FICO_Score__c
0    542
458  390
0    702
397  640

So I want to update the two zeros in FICO with the 542 and 702.

Any insights into why I'm getting this error and what I can do about it? The only time I see this error referenced on Google is having to do with POSIX datetime values.

Any assistance or ideas are appreciated.

Warm regards,

Abe

messages.body_plain:
On Wed, Feb 4, 2015 at 12:23 PM, Abe Burnett <abe.b...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I've run into this error fairly frequently and had difficulty determining why it occurs and what to do about it via Google. I also didn't see anything about what causes this error or what to do about it on the official sqldf FAQ page.
>
> The following statement generates the error: RAW() can only be applied to a 'raw', not a 'double'.
>
> sqldf(c("update dta set dta.FICO = dta.FICO_Score__c where dta.FICO = 0 and dta.FICO_Score__c != 0", "select * from dta"))
>
> What I'm trying to do is update those values in a vector where the existing value is zero and another field is not zero.
>
> My data has the form:
>
> FICO FICO_Score__c
> 0    542
> 458  390
> 0    702
> 397  640
>
> So I want to update the two zeros in FICO with the 542 and 702.
>
> Any insights into why I'm getting this error and what I can do about it? The only time I see this error referenced on Google is having to do with POSIX datetime values.
>
> Any assistance or ideas are appreciated.
>
> Warm regards,
>
> Abe

If we write 'update set FICO =' instead of 'update set dta.FICO ='
then it works for me:

dta <-
structure(list(FICO = c(0L, 458L, 0L, 397L), FICO_Score__c = c(542L,
390L, 702L, 640L)), .Names = c("FICO", "FICO_Score__c"), class =
"data.frame", row.names = c(NA,
-4L))

sqldf(c("update dta set FICO = dta.FICO_Score__c where dta.FICO = 0

and dta.FICO_Score__c != 0", "select * from dta"))

giving:

  FICO FICO_Score__c
1  542           542
2  458           390
3  702           702
4  397           640
